correctness.rationale: For every finite simple isolate-free H and every r>=0, the general antitone NOR identity f^3=f is proved and the one-cone rule is analyzed in exhaustive symbolic cases. The base distinguished basin equals 1+T(H) because f_H(x)=0 exactly for total dominating supports, and f_H(x)=all-one only for x=all-zero. Iterated cone lifting adds 2^{n+j}-1 states to that basin, one singleton fixed orbit per new hub, and preserves all other labelled basin cardinalities and periods. Both standalone direct-checking implementations passed 1,890 and 138 finite graph/attachment tests respectively, comparing complete attractor dictionaries; they are supplemental to the unrestricted proof.

value.rationale: Graph join with a clique is a canonical, highly reusable operation. The theorem preserves the full nonprincipal attraction spectrum exactly on every isolate-free graph H, while quantifying how all but r of the new configurations are concentrated in the universal zero/one oscillator. It connects that precise basin population to the natural total-domination count, proves unique basin dominance after one hub and asymptotically certain attraction as r grows. This is a structural all-graph classification and not a numerical recomputation of a known graph table.
